text: How does the Government plan to encourage stakeholders to adopt these solutions?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, we have seen that many of our existing HDB and commercial buildings have installed solar panels on their respective rooftops.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Can we know how much energy efficiency and savings have been made since the installation?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Some of my friends and cousins have been asking what does this bring to them as residents?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Ministry also share their plans for those remaining HDB blocks and do we actually target to do for all the residential properties?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: If so, what is the timeline that we aim for?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to that, is MND also planning to do this for the new HDB residential properties via the BTOs and the new buildings upcoming?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I would also like the Minister to share how can the residents know the value of the solar panels installed on top of their blocks.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This knowledge will go a long way in educating not just adults but everyone in the household.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Will HDB start to explore having solar window panels so that residents can also play their part in adopting solar consumption?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: On the commercial building front, will there be plans to move our old existing substations, with their reasonably large land spaces and even those on prime land, underground?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I understand there is, currently, an ongoing construction of an underground transmission substation, with commercial buildings above it.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Will it just stop there or will it increase progressively over time?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Buildings account for over 20% of Singapore's carbon emissions.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Therefore, green buildings will be a key lever for our net‐zero ambitions.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: How will MND and BCA continue to support our transition to green buildings and a low carbon built environment?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Also, MND announced last year that it was driving R&D in urban sustainability such that our urban infrastructure is made much more climate‐resilient while reducing carbon emissions.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Can we have an update on the progress made and how MND plans to encourage stakeholders to adopt these solutions?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Have we achieved any innovation that has the potential to be commercialised and exported to the world?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Can MND provide an update on the progress of the HDB Green Towns Programme?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I know the target for solar panel installation has been revised upwards.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: How about the targets for other aspects of the programme?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: How much have we moved beyond pilots to deploy solutions at scale?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Urban rooftop farms on multi-storey carparks will not only contribute to this movement but also bring together neighbours in a meaningful endeavour and build social cohesion.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: How will the Ministry support such farming efforts?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Will MND consider incorporating green features into our HDB flats by adopting sustainable materials and designs in future housing projects, concurrently upgrading our existing ones through the Home Improvement Programmes?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Will HDB consider appropriate greener alternatives, like installing low-heat transfer windows, to cool down our flats, thereby enabling residents to be less reliant on fans and air-conditioning and, indirectly, contribute towards saving their utility costs?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Miss Rachel Ong, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Chairman, in my house visits and conversations with residents, I have observed increasing interest amongst private estate residents, specifically condominium residents, in being engaged in sustainability efforts.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: However, access to recycling bins for different materials is limited in condominium estates.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In addition to keeping HDB estates sustainable, with the rising proportion of residents living in condominiums and other apartments over the last decade, it is vital that we also support these residents in Singapore's sustainability efforts.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Can the Ministry share future plans to support and encourage recycling efforts in private estates, especially in the condominiums?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: A 2018 study by Future Cities Laboratory found that the less-educated and less-wealthy people in Singapore are less actively engaged with urban nature, with potential negative impact for health and well-being.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Understandably, expending finances on travel to nature reserves would not be a priority for the lower income.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Many lower-income working adults also may have limited time to access nature.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: For some, the distance between their households and green spaces deters the frequency of their visits.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: With this in mind, how will the Ministry continue to improve equity in green space access for the lower-income families, especially for our children?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman, Singapore has long been known as a Garden City.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Minister please give an update on the progress made so far in transforming Singapore into a City in Nature?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Does NParks have further plans to enhance and expand Singapore’s green and blue spaces?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Ultimately, our green and blue spaces exist for our people and for future generations.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, it is important for the community to have a voice in shaping the landscapes they live and play in.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can the Ministry better collaborate and consult with the community?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What are the strategies to ensure that the amenities are kept up-to-date and the Ministry’s plans to balance competing priorities both on the islands and in the sea space surrounding it?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Ministry consider carrying out a capacity assessment to ensure our nature spaces are protected?

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
text: Chairman, climate change and sustainability education requires the teaching of not only sustainability-related skillsets, values and principles but also the ability to think ecologically and holistically at a systems level.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
text: Future generations of Singaporeans need to be both digital citizens and ecological citizens.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
text: Are efforts being undertaken to ensure teachers have access to sustainability resources and training in order to deliver such curriculum?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Poh Li San, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Mr Chairman, how is the Government preparing our teachers from Primary schools to Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) for the green economy?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Do we have a roadmap for Universities, Polytechnics, ITEs, JCs and Secondary schools to support the green economy?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: The Government will need to update the education curriculum and teaching materials for sustainability-related courses.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: What are the programmes to train and equip our teaching staff with the latest skillsets and knowledge so that, in turn, they can teach their students the same required by businesses and industries?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: In order to prepare our students for the green economy, changes will need to be made to our curriculum.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Has the Government set up a general roadmap for all our education institutions so that the design of the courses and programmes fulfil the wide-ranging demands of the green economy?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: How does MOE ensure that relevant courses, diplomas and degrees are offered in the IHLs and schools in order to prepare a pipeline of local talents to fill the jobs required for the green economy?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Considering lifelong learning now to be an integral part of Singapore’s education, the system should incorporate sustainability modules which can be picked up at all ages.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Is provision being made for such flexibility in the SkillsFuture courses and programmes?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: How will the Government facilitate collaboration between education and training institutions, research and industry stakeholders to create relevant academic, internship and apprenticeship in sustainability-related industries?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: Chairman, in my speech supporting the second Parliamentary Motion on Climate Change earlier this January, I highlighted the need for our IHLs to enhance their course offerings in PET to better integrate sustainability-focused and related modules.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: This is because, with the greening of jobs over time, increasing fields of disciplines will need to embrace sustainability in their practice.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: I also shared on the need to better complement PET curricula with CET Sustainability Modules to ensure that, by the time our students graduate, they are equipped with up-to-date skills and knowledge required for their fields.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Chairman, the lack of understanding of sustainability-related concepts has been a barrier to galvanising strong action.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Our students, workers and businesses can seize opportunities in the green economy if equipped with the proper understanding of climate change and sustainable development.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: We should prepare them to grasp the science of global warming and the current and impending impact of climate change in their respective fields of work.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: We should enable them to position themselves to be the change needed in the world.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: First, the challenges of sustainability can only be overcomed through the involvement of future generations.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Our schools can play a fundamental role in enhancing our children's eco-literacy and nurture them to be stewards of our environment.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Our universities are well-positioned to be the key enablers for the development of the green economy in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: So, what governance and accountability framework will be put in place to determine and monitor the spending of green R&D as well as to assess outcomes?

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, climate change is a real and existential threat.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The latest findings from Work Group 2 of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)'s Sixth Assessment Report, which were released last week, assessed that the impacts of climate change are more apparent and will affect us more severely than previously thought.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are already seeing some of these effects – stronger and longer heat waves, unprecedented droughts and floods, rising sea-levels and storm surges affecting communities all over the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In the past year, international resolve to take urgent and decisive action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions has grown.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In November 2021, as part of the 2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP26) Glasgow Climate Pact, it was agreed that all Parties should aim to achieve global net-zero emissions by mid-century, in order to keep the 1.5-degree goal within reach.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Members of this House have also called for more decisive action on climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Indeed, since 2021, this House has debated two Motions on climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This House has acknowledged climate change as a global emergency and called on the Government to accelerate efforts against climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Members made several suggestions, including increasing the carbon tax substantially, green financing, creating green jobs and strengthening corporate accountability.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore has taken important steps to contribute to the global effort to tackle climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Poh Li San, Mr Louis Chua, Mr Louis Ng and Prof Koh Lian Pin asked about Singapore's key considerations and the process for setting our climate targets and the timeframe.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In our LEDS two years ago, we laid out three thrusts to achieve our aspiration: first, transforming our industry, economy and society; second, harnessing low-carbon technologies; and third, pursuing international collaboration, for example, in the form of carbon markets and electricity imports.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We said that we would continue to review our climate goals with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions as soon as viable.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: If the potential emissions reductions from each of these thrusts are available sooner, we will be able to realise our goals earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Chairman, since then, there have been important developments at COP26 in Glasgow.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: More countries pledged to reach net-zero by mid-century.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This will spur greater investment in low-carbon solutions, making them technologically and economically viable earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Paris Agreement's Article 6 rulebook for international carbon markets was also finalised.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Chairman, this is a significant improvement over our current LEDS.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are making a decisive move: one that is necessary, practical and implementable.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are making a commitment on behalf of generations of Singaporeans to come, spanning several decades into the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I am glad that Members from both sides of this House support these moves.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Before we finalise our plans and declare a specific net-zero year, we will consult closely with industry and citizen stakeholder groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This is because raising climate ambition will not only bring about many benefits but also entail some costs and trade-offs.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: These engagements will take place under the Green Plan and our broader SG Together movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: COP26 successfully finalised the rulebook for international carbon markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Carbon markets allow Singapore to access global mitigation opportunities through international carbon credits and provide an additional option for us to decarbonise.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: They enhance the transparency of international carbon trading and provide the necessary quality assurance for Singapore to use high-quality international carbon credits to help meet our climate goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I agree with Mr Henry Kwek on the need to strike the right balance between pursuing domestic mitigation and using carbon credits.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As we strive to reach net-zero earlier, we will need to do both.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We will continue to prioritise domestic efforts to meet our climate goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: However, as a small, alternative energy-disadvantaged city state, we will need to look beyond purely domestic mitigation and consider other measures, such as importing low-carbon hydrogen and carbon capture, utilisation and storage, which are reliant on international cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Carbon credits will help offset our residual emissions to reach net-zero and, at the same time, spur the development of high-quality carbon markets in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Second, major countries and companies are making substantial investments in decarbonisation technologies, making them technologically and economically viable earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: These investments in low-carbon solutions will drive down costs and accelerate technical viability and commercial scalability, allowing us to lower our emissions earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The third reason why we can: more global corporates are making commitments to reduce emissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: When the global Climate Ambition Alliance was launched at COP25 in 2019, fewer than 100 companies committed to net-zero by 2050.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: But, just two years later, in 2021, some 5,000 companies had committed to net-zero – a significant 50-fold increase, which, we expect, will increase further.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Private financing is also shifting towards sustainability and low-carbon projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Sustainable private financing and corporate net-zero targets have a powerful mutually reinforcing effect.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: They draw capital towards sustainable projects and make it more difficult and expensive to finance projects which are not.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This will not only accelerate global emissions reduction but also provide capital to create new economic opportunities in the global green economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: With these positive international developments, we now have confidence that Singapore can more effectively find solutions to address our alternative energy constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We cannot wish these constraints away, but we now have more options to enable us to reach net-zero earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Chairman, I have just explained why we now can move decisively to net-zero.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I will explain why we should make a decisive shift.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We want to take advantage of the positive global trends in sustainable financing and corporate net-zero targets to make Singapore an attractive place for green economic activities in industry, services and finance.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This will reposition our economy and establish our competitive edge early in a low-carbon future.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Manufacturing makes up about 20% of our GDP and offers many good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The world is moving away from traditional carbon-intensive industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: For example, the energy and chemicals sector is itself re-orientating to pursue sustainable production and new areas of growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Singapore is positioning itself as a first mover to capture these opportunities and jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In November last year, our Economic Development Board (EDB) announced the Sustainable Jurong Island plan to transform Jurong Island into a Sustainable Energy and Chemicals Park that makes and exports sustainable products globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are also moving ahead with plans to be a hub for sustainable aviation fuels and, in the future, for hydrogen.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Several major companies which already have a strong presence here have committed to making major investments in their operations and products to align with our mutual goals for zero emissions by mid-century.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We hope to attract new companies, too, which share our sustainable net-zero ambition.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are building the capabilities to catalyse sustainable and green finance in the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Global sales of green bonds grew from nearly nothing in 2012 to S$380 billion in 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Institute of Banking and Finance Singapore have set out 12 technical skills and competencies in sustainable finance to help financial institutions and training providers promote careers in sustainability and climate change-related jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are developing Singapore as an international carbon trading and services hub with Singapore-based global carbon exchanges, such as Climate Impact X and AirCarbon Exchange.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We will continue to develop the larger ecosystem by anchoring key activities, such as project development, financing and certification, in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We will signal to global markets and corporates that Singapore is ready to be a good partner and location for forward-looking companies which have clear low-carbon goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This will create many good jobs for Singaporeans and enhance Singapore's value proposition in the future low-carbon global economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Don Wee, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Miss Cheryl Chan asked how the revised carbon tax levels will support our green transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As we make a decisive shift towards a low-carbon future, we need to provide the right price signal to shape responsible behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We have always priced key resources like water, energy and waste disposal properly so that consumers and businesses make appropriate decisions, taking the true costs into account.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In the same way, the revised carbon tax levels will provide the appropriate carbon price signal for individuals and businesses to internalise the cost of carbon emissions in their consumption and business decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In Parliament last February, Members proposed raising the carbon tax, with suggestions ranging from $30 to $133 per tonne of emissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I am glad that during the discussions of these two Motions this past year and, during this Budget session, Members from both sides of this House have so strongly spoken in support of a significant carbon tax.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Members may also access these materials through the SG Parl MP mobile app.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Announcing our intentions and the expected trajectory early provides predictability for investment decisions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We also take reference from the carbon price levels of competitor jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: China and South Korea, which submitted net-zero pledges within the last two years, have sizeable emissions-intensive sectors and export to our region as well.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: But we should bear in mind that they have a range of renewable alternatives, including nuclear, which is not available to us in this timeframe.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The 2030 projected carbon price for the European Union (EU) is about S$174 per tonne.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The EU has legacy emissions-intensive sectors, some of which are still reliant on coal that will require considerable effort to decarbonise.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Another useful reference is the internal carbon prices that many corporates are already using to make their medium- to long-term business and investment decisions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: For example, the multinational consumer goods company Unilever already currently uses an internal carbon price of S$77 per tonne and Temasek uses an internal carbon price of S$57 per tonne currently.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: An appropriate carbon price will shape responsible behaviour.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Individuals and households will have a greater incentive to adopt more sustainable lifestyles, such as conserving electricity and using more energy-efficient appliances.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The savings from these changes will offset the increases in utility charges.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The carbon tax will also provide the impetus for businesses to be more resource-efficient and invest in decarbonisation solutions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Mr Don Wee, Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Miss Cheryl Chan asked how the Government will help minimise the impact of carbon tax on households and businesses and account for the use of the revenue collected from the carbon tax.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The Government will flow the additional tax collected back to help households and businesses transition to a low-carbon future.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Nine hundred and fifty thousand households have already benefited from U-Save rebates from 2019 to 2021, and we will provide additional support to help households manage the cost of utilities.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: But saving energy, and not just helping to pay the bills, is an even more important way to lower emissions and household utility bills.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: All in, Mr Chairman, almost a million households and more than 200 businesses have already benefited from these schemes that we have implemented over the years.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The carbon tax will fund additional schemes to support households and businesses to achieve greater carbon efficiency and decarbonisation, and these schemes will be subject to the usual stringent governance and accountability frameworks and key performance indicators (KPIs) for the use of public funds.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We recognise that it will not be easy for the emissions-intensive trade-exposed sectors to fully decarbonise their emissions in the near to medium-term while remaining competitive with other manufacturing locations.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Therefore, we will also use the carbon tax collected to provide transitory support for existing investments which have contributed to the current and earlier phases of Singapore's economic growth.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This will give them time to make the transition to a low-carbon economy without blunting the price signal and being very clear about what our trajectory is.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Mr Louis Ng asked to expand the coverage of the carbon tax to include all reportable facilities.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: At this point in time, we will retain the threshold of 25,000 tonnes of emissions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This covers about 80% of our emissions and is already one of the highest in the world.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Coupled with our existing taxes on transport fuels, we are achieving around 90% coverage.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Lowering the threshold would impose significant additional regulatory burden and costs on companies, without any meaningful increase in coverage.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked how we can catalyse the purchase of high-quality carbon credits.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Providing companies with the flexibility to surrender high-quality international carbon credits to offset up to 5% of their taxable emissions will help to create local demand for high-quality carbon credits and catalyse the development of a carbon services hub in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It will also cushion the impact for companies that are able to source for cost-effective and credible carbon credits.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We will have clear environmental integrity criteria to ensure that the carbon credits surrendered by businesses to offset their emissions are aligned with international carbon market rules finalised at COP26 and reflect an actual reduction in global emissions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Mr Chairman, the carbon tax is but one part of our comprehensive package of measures to move our nation decisively towards a low-carbon future.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Last year, we launched the Green Plan, a whole-of-nation movement to advance our national agenda on sustainable development.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: By moving decisively now, we are charting the path to a cleaner, greener Singapore for our future generations – with a sustainable environment and lifestyles, a forward-looking economy with new green jobs, and a brighter future at the forefront of a low-carbon world.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: One year ago, we launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030 to catalyse a nationwide sustainability movement to move towards a greener future.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Since then, the international momentum for climate action has increased.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean spoke about the greater urgency and resolve internationally to take decisive action and why Singapore will raise our climate ambitions to achieve net-zero emissions by or around mid-century.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: He explained how carbon pricing will be pivotal in spurring Singapore's green transition.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore must catch and ride the green wave to thrive in a low-carbon future.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is key to our continued relevance as an international hub for transport, business and finance.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The sustainability movement in Singapore is growing and inspiring action across all segments of society.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Ms Poh Li San and Ms Rachel Ong will be heartened to hear that we have made progress in many areas under the Green Plan, including the following.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: GreenGov.SG was launched to steer the public sector towards ambitious sustainability targets.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Organisations, such as Sentosa Development Corporation, Nanyang Technological University and Khoo Teck Puat Hospital, have drawn up their own sustainability plans.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have been engaging our partners from the people, private and public, or 3P sectors, to make the Green Plan a reality, as raised by Ms Janet Ang.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Green Plan Ministries have engaged more than 25,000 stakeholders over the past year, including corporates, youths, NGOs and the community.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They have participated in initiatives, such as the OneMillionTrees movement, Green Plan Conversations and the Youth Action Challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The private sector is adopting sustainability practices and committing resources to secure an early foothold in the green transition.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Maritime and Aviation sectors are trialling the use of cleaner and lower-carbon fuels.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Global firms, such as McKinsey, Bain and Company, and PwC, have established sustainability hubs and centres in Singapore, to serve the region and beyond.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Civil society, community organisations and youths are galvanising a social movement on sustainability, empowering action and advocacy from the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: At last year’s Climate Action Week, over 60 partners from the 3P sectors organised more than 130 wide-ranging activities, a record for the event.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To mark Youth Day at the 26th United Nations Climate Change Conference, a group of Singaporeans and youth-led environmental and climate organisations, such as Ho Xiang Tian and FiTree, released a statement with wide-ranging recommendations on tackling climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I am inspired by their passion to drive change and encourage our youths to continue to advocate and act for change.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As we step towards a greener and low-carbon future, we will need to build a new social compact to prepare for changes in the way we live, work and play.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As citizens, we must reflect on the changes we are willing to make to our lifestyles.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Across the economy, we must move boldly to transform and capture the opportunities from the green transition.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As a nation, we must thoroughly debate the trade-offs and come to a consensus on the right balance to strike.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Today, my colleagues and I will give an update on how the Government is preparing for the transition to a low-carbon future, anchored around the Green Plan.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Minister Gan Kim Yong will elaborate on our efforts to grow our green economy and decarbonise our energy sector.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Minister S Iswaran will speak about measures to further reduce carbon emissions in the transport sector.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Minister Desmond Lee will share about our progress in greening our built environment and in transforming Singapore into a City in Nature.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Minister Chan Chun Sing will give an update on how we are nurturing the next generation to be stewards in environmental sustainability and how our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) are driving skills training, research and innovation in sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Improving energy efficiency is one of the primary ways that businesses can lower their carbon emission.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will provide targeted support to help every sector decarbonise.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: BCA will support the built environment sector; EMA the power generation sector; and EDB and NEA, the manufacturing sector.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin asked about the Energy Efficiency Fund, which is part of an enhanced package of support launched in January 2019 to help industries become more energy efficient and lower their carbon tax.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Since then, we have committed over $75 million to support businesses to implement energy efficiency improvement and carbon abatement projects.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They are at the heart of our economy, supplying products and services to many sectors and employing a significant proportion of our workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: While many of them are nimble, dynamic and creative, they often lack resources to invest in energy-efficient technologies or make changes to their business.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Earlier in the Budget debate, Mr Don Wee and Ms Denise Phua called for more support for SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Over the years, we have built on our support for SMEs to achieve greater energy efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Last year, NEA and ESG supported the Carbon Pricing Leadership Coalition Singapore’s LowCarbonSG initiative to help companies build capabilities in measuring, monitoring and reducing their carbon emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA and the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) set up an Energy Efficiency Technology Centre (EETC) in 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It provides SMEs with low-cost energy assessments to help them identify opportunities to improve energy efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Centre also develops the workforce by training students and practitioners in industrial energy efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA is working with SIT to strengthen the Centre’s capabilities in the next phase.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Enhancements will include setting up a training-and-simulation centre to enable learners to practise their craft in a realistic, yet safe environment.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With the enhancements, the Centre will be able to assume a more prominent role in Singapore’s transition to a low-carbon economy.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NEA’s Energy Efficiency Fund (E2F) helps SMEs in the manufacturing sector to defray the cost of adopting energy-efficient technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Kawarin Enterprise Pte Ltd, a local steel manufacturing company, has benefited from the Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: By upgrading their old air compressors to more energy-efficient ones, they enjoyed annual cost savings of more than $30,000 and abated about 48 tonnes of carbon annually.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will help companies invest in energy-efficient equipment, such as lighting, air-conditioning, boilers and air compressors.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will simplify the grant application and disbursement process.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I urge companies to take advantage of the higher support level early.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The green transition will present new opportunities for our economy and workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We hope to anchor emerging green industries in Singapore to create good jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are growing a new industry in agri-tech.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Minister of State Desmond Tan has shared this in his speech.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mature industries, such as the environmental services industry, are poised for transformation, catalysing higher demand for green skills.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will support our workers to develop these skills.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Eu Leng Pheng, who began his career in the chemical and marine industry, took a leap of faith and entered the waste management industry in 2017, as a Facilities Manager in LHT Holdings to support wood waste recycling operations.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To make the transition, he took part in a professional course offered by the Waste Management and Recycling Association of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: His vast experience in troubleshooting electrical components and circuit boards from his previous work experience allowed him to quickly render professional support to other engineers.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: He has also provided in-house training to the mechanics in his company, furthering their knowledge.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are also encouraging households to embrace sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Eligible households can redeem $225 worth of e-vouchers to offset costs for energy-efficient refrigerators, LED lights and water-efficient shower fittings.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The vouchers are valid till 31 December 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I urge eligible households to use these vouchers when your appliances are due for replacement.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Making the switch can help households save on utility bills.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Second, we will continue to invest in science and technology to unlock possibilities for a low-carbon future.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our water story is a good example of the critical role R&D plays in Singapore’s development.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In our decades of patient and persistent investments, over the years, we have created two of our national taps, NEWater and desalinated water, and raised Singapore’s profile as a leading global hydrohub.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our research objective now is to bring down the energy requirement through science and technology.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2023, a Desalination Integrated Validation Plant will be commissioned to trial promising technologies to reduce the energy consumption of desalination to less than two kilowatt hours per cubic metre (kWh/m3) of water.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will pave the way for the technologies to be implemented in full-scale desalination plants.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The plant is just one of the many projects that are supported under our national Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2025 plan.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Ms Poh Li San and Prof Koh Lian Pin have pointed out, science and technology are important enablers for the Green Plan.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Eighty million dollars will be allocated to Closing the Resource Loop, to develop sustainable resource recovery solutions for key waste streams, such as e-waste, plastics and food.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It will support the development of useful and safe applications for treated waste residue and low-carbon waste treatment options.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will build on the $45 million Closing the Waste Loop under RIE2020.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Under this funding initiative, NEA has funded 15 R&D projects, with seven garnering commercial interest.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The remaining budget was allocated to the Competitive Funding for Water Research programme last year.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our investments will go towards developing high-impact solutions for our national water needs.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: But beyond that, research and innovation will also be an engine for green growth, spurring private sector R&D spending, job creation and technology spin-offs in the water industry and adjacent sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, NEWRI has developed technologies with local and global applications in areas, such as biomimetic membranes for desalination and anchored investments from global companies in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Science and technology will also inform our policies and interventions to keep Singapore liveable in the face of climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As Mr Leon Perera pointed out, rising urban temperatures is a major concern for our compact and dense city.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government already incorporates urban planning measures to keep neighbourhoods cool.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, weaving nature more intensively into our built environment, which Minister Desmond Lee will touch on later.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are also working with MOH, MOM and the Workplace Safety and Health Council, to ensure that guidelines on managing heat stress at workplaces are regularly updated.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We need to involve the whole-of-society in the sustainability movement and develop a shared ownership of our environment.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin and Ms Hany Soh asked for an update on the SG Eco Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have seen great interest since its launch in November 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This includes 42 smaller projects under the new Sprout category, which has a simpler application process.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Some of the recipients in the second grant call are: Earth School Singapore, which has launched a new experiential education programme for Primary school students; U Farm, a social enterprise farm, which will train and employ persons with disabilities and host environmental programmes for the public; Mr Neo Zhi Xuan and his team, who will develop a web application to educate the public on where and how to recycle different household items.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our applicants have diverse interests and goals, reflecting the reach of the grant.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will work with our grant recipients to maximise the impact of their projects and co-create relevant environmental and community engagement targets.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: SG Eco Fund will also explore new partnerships to rally more people to contribute to the Green Plan.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our local communities are also responding to the call to action.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Don Wee asked about the progress of Eco Towns.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In Tampines, Semula, a social enterprise, will be conducting plastic collection drives at F&B outlets and shopping malls and involving the community to process the collected plastics into art pieces.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In Nee Soon South, the grassroots organisation is setting up a Black Soldier Flies composting hub.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In Chua Chu Kang and Hong Kah North, grassroots leaders have organised hackathons with residents to co-develop an Eco Town plan for the district.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We intend to provide more support, including capacity building workshops, to help more communities in Singapore plan and develop sustainability initiatives in their towns.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will complement HDB's Green Towns Programme to enhance the sustainability of estates.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will continue to consult and engage the public on environment and climate issues, including our net-zero ambition, as Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean has explained.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin suggested that sufficient time must be set aside for the public to learn about the issues and share their views.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Under the SG Together movement, we created many opportunities for Singaporeans to participate and contribute actively to sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Depending on the issue at hand, different approaches and modalities are adopted to engage stakeholders and we endeavour to share the insights gathered from these consultations with the public.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Across the Public Service, we are also growing capabilities to engage well and consistently, through shared frameworks, case studies and ongoing training.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For instance, the disposable carrier bag charge was developed after more than one year of extensive consultations and engagements with the industry and the public, including a Citizens' Workgroup.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MSE and NEA released our response to the recommendations by the Citizens' Workgroup in 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For the Lim Chu Kang Masterplan, we brought stakeholders together over six months to discuss how the Lim Chu Kang area could be redeveloped to become our agri-food production hub of the future.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The full report covering the whole engagement series has just been finalised and will be published soon.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These consultations and engagements enable participants and stakeholders, including the Government, to hear and understand diverse views.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Participants go away with a better appreciation of different perspectives and the rationale for policies, and the Government goes away with better-informed and considered decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It is my hope that the Green Plan will spark new possibilities that were once thought to be unattainable.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: That it will pave the way for a greener, brighter future.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Chairman, I am encouraged by Members' commitment to sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many have spoken about it and asked how we can do more to further our sustainability and climate ambition.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Members also recognise that while Singapore must take bold steps to address climate change, we must remain pragmatic, managing the trade-offs for supporting our enterprises and helping our workers in the green transition.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A few days ago, I outlined in this House our economic strategies for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, we need to press on with our efforts to help our industries and enterprises decarbonise.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, we need to help our enterprises and workforce harness sustainability as a competitive advantage, invest in innovation and seize new growth opportunities in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And third, we need to expand Singapore's global connection to capture cross-border opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Singapore's transition to a low-carbon economy is critical not only to ensure that we are aligned with the global efforts on sustainable development, but also to leverage new opportunities in the emerging green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Today, I will focus on Government's Green Economy Strategy and I will cover four key areas.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, decarbonise our industries, including the energy sector, which is a major emitter.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, drive new areas of growth in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Third, invest in the development of new low-carbon solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, let me talk about decarbonising our industries and the energy sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many companies have already embarked on the sustainability journey, for they know that not doing so would risk them losing relevance and market share.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue to support industries and enterprises in their transition efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Last November, we released the Sustainable Jurong Island report which outlines our plan to transform Jurong Island into a Sustainable Energy and Chemicals Park.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Park will operate sustainably and produce sustainable products for exports.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, Shell Singapore has announced plans to halve its operational emissions by 2030 from 2016 levels.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Another example is specialty materials manufacturer, Arkema, which will be setting up a new bio-factory on Jurong Island to produce high-performance polymers made from castor beans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The new plant will enable Arkema to increase its polymer production capacity by 50% to meet the rising global demand for sustainable, high-performance materials.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Decarbonising Singapore's energy sector is key in greening Singapore's economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The demand for energy will grow as we digitalise our economy and electrify our transport and various processes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, the energy transition is especially challenging for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many of the renewable energy options adopted by other countries are not available to us.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have little wind, hydro or tidal power.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Solar is our most viable form of renewable energy, but we have heavy cloud cover and limited land available to expand our solar energy deployment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Despite these limitations and complexities, we must continue to forge ahead to transform the energy sector and reduce its carbon footprint.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, we will enhance the energy efficiency of power generation plants.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Last year, we launched the second Genco Energy Efficiency (Genco EE) Grant Call to support generation companies in improving the efficiency of their existing power plants.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: EMA is evaluating the proposals and will announce the successful applicants later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We also amended the Electricity Act to empower EMA to require electricity generation licensees to meet greenhouse gas emissions standards.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: EMA will consult the industry on the specific standards later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are finding ways to further accelerate solar deployment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our public sector agencies are taking the lead in solar deployment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: HDB, for example, recently launched the seventh SolarNova tender, to aggregate demand across HDB blocks and Government sites.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Since 2020, JTC has also put in place a mandatory solar deployment scheme for its lessees.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And to-date, over 224 MWp of solar has been deployed across JTC's industrial estates or around 40% of our total solar deployment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are also exploring how we can overcome our land constraints.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, PSA has installed vertical solar panels on its external walls of the PSA Tuas Port Maintenance Base Admin Building as a trial.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Government is also exploring the use of vertical solar panels on other surfaces.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To further expand the potential of solar deployment in Singapore, EMA is looking at ways to integrate energy storage systems into the grid, to overcome the intermittency of solar energy and manage the stability and resilience of our energy grid.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Increasing the energy efficiency of our natural gas power plants can, at best, reduce carbon emissions by about 10%.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even if we maximise all available space in Singapore for solar deployment and account for efficiency improvements, we would still be unable to generate enough power to keep the lights on with solar energy alone.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Meaningful abatement can only be achieved through tapping on renewable energy beyond our shores and by developing the use of other low-carbon alternatives in the longer term.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The energy transition will require trade-offs and we will need to accept changes to the way we live and work.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In particular, the transition to more carbon-efficient generation and low-carbon technologies, accelerating the deployment of renewable energy and importing electricity, may not mean cheaper electricity, as Mr Shawn Huang pointed out.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will need to invest in infrastructure and technology which will be costly and are likely to lead to higher electricity costs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is an inevitable but necessary trade-off to build a better and greener world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Government is pacing and managing the transition to ensure that electricity remains affordable and will provide assistance to vulnerable groups when necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue to work closely with our industry partners and stakeholders to innovate and explore new solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even as we push on with decarbonisation, there are exciting new economic opportunities, too.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They are different sides of the same coin on sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Green financing, for example, will grow as companies look to financing instruments to support their sustainable investments.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Another opportunity is in the carbon services and carbon credits market.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Firms and even countries will want to trade in carbon credits to offset their emissions and meet their climate goals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Leon Perera suggested that we need to scrutinise and properly account for the carbon credits and, indeed, so.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This also means that we will need monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) services.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These growth areas will lead to good jobs in the professional services.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked how the Government will enable the development of Singapore's carbon markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue to work with the private sector, as well as with other countries, to develop carbon credit projects which have high environmental integrity and quality, as Mr Leon Perera talked about.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These credits can be traded via trusted platforms in Singapore or can be used by corporates or the Government to meet climate targets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, we have partnered local ecosystem players, such as Climate Impact X (CIX) and AirCarbon Exchange (ACX), to establish marketplaces for companies to access high-quality carbon credits.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This entire value chain and ecosystem will require new skills.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOM, MOE, Workforce Singapore (WSG) and SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) are working together to equip our workers with these new skills and for these new job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Another area that presents opportunities for Singapore is sustainable tourism.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Eventually, global tourism will recover and become vibrant again as we emerge from the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Tourists are increasingly demanding sustainable travel options, such as eco-friendly hotels and attractions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is why we have been taking steps to work with the tourism industry to move towards more sustainable operations, create sustainable products and experiences for our visitors to establish Singapore as a sustainable urban destination.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This includes initiatives, such as the launch of the hotel sustainability roadmap later this month.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is a key milestone that will spur hotels to adopt sustainable operations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Last year, Sentosa received the Top 100 Destination Sustainability Stories Award.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Sentosa Development Corporation (SDC) also launched the Sentosa Carbon Neutral Network, Singapore's first business alliance committed to carbon neutrality by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The network aims to help businesses develop sustainability solutions through the sharing of resources and expertise while also leveraging economies of scale and providing a common network to introduce larger-scale precinct level solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I agree with Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Ms Foo Mee Har that businesses which start early on the sustainability journey can gain a competitive advantage over those which are slow to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is why, last year, the Government launched the Enterprise Sustainability Programme (ESP) to enable local enterprises to uplift their capabilities and capture opportunities in sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, to develop sustainability capabilities in enterprises through training and access to relevant tools and resources.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, to strengthen sector-specific initiatives through partnerships with Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) and corporates.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And third, to foster a vibrant and conducive sustainability ecosystem by working with service providers and enablers in training, certification and provision of green financing.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Businesses are also making good use of the Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS) - Green, which provides enterprises better access to green financing.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The loan will enable the Singapore tech company to accelerate the development and distribution of its high-tech energy storage solutions using lithium-ion batteries for the Tuas Port's automated guided vehicle fleet.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I encourage more companies to tap on the ESP and EFS-Green.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Chairman, as Ms Foo Mee Har and Ms Jessica Tan pointed out, innovation and the development of low-carbon solutions are key to sharpening Singapore's competitive advantage in the green economy and facilitating the energy transition.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some of these solutions, such as low-carbon hydrogen and carbon capture, utilisation and storage, or CCUS, have the potential to be a gamechanger, especially for the hard-to-abate sectors, such as energy and chemicals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, the technology will take time to mature and become more commercially viable.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Government is studying how we can catalyse the development.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many of the technologies required to enable the production, transportation, storage and use of hydrogen at scale are still nascent and relatively costly today.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Currently, there are also no commercially available utility-scale combined cycle gas turbines (CCGTs) that can use 100% hydrogen.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Without significant retrofitting, only small amounts of hydrogen up to 5% by volume can be deployed.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Another challenge is in transporting hydrogen in larger volumes over long distances as the technology to transport liquified hydrogen is not yet available.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Alternative carrier forms of hydrogen, such as ammonia and liquid organic hydride carriers, are more easily transported but come with their own challenges, such as the need to extract the hydrogen from the carriers at the destination.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We expect the costs of low-carbon hydrogen technologies to fall over time with technological advancements and greater economies of scale.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Low-carbon hydrogen will also become increasingly more accessible with the development of global supply chains and as technological developments make its transportation and use easier.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Government is, therefore, investing resources to understand and monitor the potential for hydrogen deployment in Singapore and exploring potential solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One of the projects supported involves NTU working with a consortium of companies comprising local enterprises, such as PSA and Sembcorp Industries, and international partners like Chiyoda Corporation and Mitsubishi Corporation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The consortium will seek to develop new technologies for the extraction of hydrogen from liquid organic hydrogen carriers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Another project involves NUS and NTU researchers collaborating with the industry to develop new catalysts to liberate hydrogen from ammonia in a more energy-efficient way.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These have the potential to allow for more efficient and economical transport of hydrogen, which can, in turn, contribute to the expansion of global hydrogen supply chains and improve the viability of hydrogen as an alternative fuel.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Another promising low-carbon technology is CCUS, which could be deployed to capture greenhouse gas emissions and keep them out of the atmosphere.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Efforts are underway to make CCUS pathways a reality and we will put in place a robust verification system to ensure proper accounting of the carbon captured, as Mr Leon Perera mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
