text: CCUTT will facilitate the rapid evaluation and test-bedding of emerging carbon capture and utilisation technologies to accelerate industry adoption.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will complement our efforts to develop Jurong Island into a sustainable E&C park.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To enhance the synergy of our R&D efforts in low-carbon technologies and solutions, A*STAR will reorganise key R&D capabilities across its institutes into a new Institute of Sustainability for Chemicals, Energy and Environment, or ISCE2.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: ISCE2 will advance research areas, such as carbon capture and utilisation, low-carbon hydrogen, carbon life-cycle accounting and synthetic biology, to pave the way for alternative green materials, products and processes to support Singapore's sustainability agenda.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: ISCE2 will continue to partner academia, public agencies and industry to contribute to Singapore's climate change goals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We look forward to reaping the fruits of these industry and international partnerships in time to come.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I shared about the reskilling and upskilling programmes offered by agencies in January.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include the Career Conversion Programme (CCP) for Clean and Renewable Energy Professionals by WSG and MAS' setting up of centres of excellence for training and research in green financing.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am pleased to hear of employers and workers coming forward to make use of these skills programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One such example is Mr Wang Yi Tian, a design engineer at SembCorp Marine (SCM).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will enable our workers to benefit from the emerging green economy and low-carbon power sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Chairman, over the past five decades, Singapore's economy has built up significant strengths and competitive advantages.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have adapted to the various challenges and constantly reinvented ourselves to stay relevant in the regional and global economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our transformation to a low-carbon economy is yet another chapter in the Singapore story.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It will be a challenging journey but an exciting one.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Government will partner our industries, businesses and workers as we undertake this journey.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Together, we can navigate the transition, explore new ideas and forge new frontiers as we create a greener future for Singapore and for the world.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Chairman, the Singapore Green Plan articulates our national climate ambitions, as well as our commitment to climate action and achieving net-zero emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The cost of solutions will be incurred by individuals, enterprises and economies, while the benefits will take time and accrue to the global community.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But we must act now, individually and collectively, by making responsible choices and trade-offs to avert a tragedy of the commons and prevent grave harm to our environment.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Over the decades, we have taken significant steps to build an efficient and sustainable transport system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We have, progressively, introduced policies on car ownership and usage, invested heavily in public transport and active mobility and promoted the transition to cleaner-energy vehicles.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It is an ambitious goal that will require policy moves, new technologies and behavioural shifts across our land transport system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Along with the decarbonisation of the power grid, electrification of vehicles is a key initiative that will have a material impact and I would like to elaborate on our moves in that regard.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Globally, EV technology continues to advance and sales of electric cars have gained momentum.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This is a promising indicator of the impact of our measures, such as the EV Early Adoption Incentive (EEAI) for cars, which has been highlighted by Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Louis Chua.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will monitor developments and assess the need for similar measures in other vehicle segments, like electric motorcycles.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To sustain the momentum of our EV transition, we will step up our efforts in three key areas.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Several Members have highlighted the need for charging infrastructure to keep pace with, if not be ahead of, EV adoption.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In practice, the average driver in Singapore may need to fully charge her electric car only once every five to seven days, given that most have a range of at least 300 kilometres.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Nevertheless, this concern over nascent technology is understandable.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To take anxiety out of range, chargers must be widely available.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Last year, MOT shared plans to deploy 60,000 charging points across public and private carparks by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Since then, LTA has undertaken a major survey of the switchrooms and substations serving residential carparks across the island to assess the additional electrical capacity needed to support EV charging.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This evaluation has given us the confidence to accelerate the implementation of our plans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will make every HDB town EV-ready by 2025.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To achieve this, we will install charging points in nearly 2,000 HDB carparks over the next three to four years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They will mostly provide low-powered, overnight charging, which would meet the needs of car owners and minimise the load on the electrical grid.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: There will be at least three charging points per carpark and more where there is demand and adequate electrical capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: LTA will launch the large-scale tender for charging points at HDB carparks in the first half of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We have also made progress in the deployment of chargers at other premises.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng’s question was regarding the pattern of ownership.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: More than 80% of electric car users live in private residences today, many in condominiums and private apartments.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, to incentivise non-landed private residences to install chargers in their carparks, we introduced the EV Common Charger Grant last July.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So far, 12 developments have used this grant and at least 20 others are in the pipeline.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Their applications are being processed and I would like to encourage more Management Corporation Strata Titles (MCSTs) to benefit from this scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our second move is to upgrade the supporting electrical infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Consumer switch-rooms and substations will have to be expanded to support increasing use of the residential charging network.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: After industry consultation and feedback, we have decided that the Government will undertake this long-term infrastructure programme.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The National EV Centre at LTA will take the lead, working with other Government agencies like EMA and HDB.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Upgrades will commence over the next few years and continue well into the 2030s.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: LTA will be issuing green bonds to fund these infrastructure upgrades.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The bond repayment obligations will be met through a tariff on EV charging operators and users, which will be phased in at a later stage.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The third thrust of our EV masterplan is to implement policies and regulations that support adoption and ensure safety.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I agree with Prof Koh Lian Pin that robust regulations and standards are necessary to ensure a reliable and safe EV charging ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To that end, LTA has worked closely with the industry on revisions to Technical Reference 25, or TR25, which is our national EV charging standard.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The revised TR25 will preserve public safety while easing compliance and maintenance obligations for owners of EV chargers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It will also allow for new technologies, such as battery-swapping, for electric motorcycles and very high-powered charging of up to 500 kilowatts.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Gan Thiam Poh have asked about our approach to such technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As they are still relatively nascent, we will focus on safety regulations, while monitoring industry and technology developments to assess their applicability to our overall charging network.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To lay the foundation for a new regulatory framework, we will introduce legislation to regulate EV charging.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This will cover the approval and registration of EV chargers and the licensing of EV charging operators.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It will also mandate the provision of charging infrastructure in new buildings and major redevelopments.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: There will be a public consultation on the proposed legislation later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We have also reviewed our vehicle policies to ensure they are relevant for an EV future.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: With the changes over the last two years, the road tax for mass market electric cars is now comparable to that of equivalent internal combustion engine (ICE) cars.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Several Members, in this debate and before, have suggested using pricing and other incentives to increase the attractiveness of EVs vis-à-vis ICE cars.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We earlier introduced the EEAI to reduce the gap in upfront costs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: However, the cost differential remains for certain mass market EVs because they fall within Category B COEs, along with bigger ICE cars.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: One reason for this is the Maximum Power Output (MPO) criterion.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We introduced the criterion of 97 kilowatts in 2013, in addition to an engine capacity of 1,600 cc or less, for Category A cars.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: That was to address the market trend then, when many luxury petrol cars with smaller but turbo-charged engines could draw on Category A COEs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Introducing the 97-kilowatt MPO threshold shifted these turbo-charged luxury cars into Category B.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: However, mass-market electric cars in international markets tend to have a MPO of 110 kilowatts or lower.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Locally, more mass-market EV models with an MPO above 97 kilowatts have been introduced in the last year.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Chairman, the EV transition also applies to other vehicle segments.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about the plans for the public transport and point-to-point (P2P) fleets.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The P2P sector is key to emissions reduction as taxis and private hire cars clock a much higher daily mileage, compared to the average private vehicles.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our taxi operators have already announced some plans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: ComfortDelgro will roll out up to 400 electric taxis, or e-taxis, in 2022, while Strides has committed to a fully electric fleet by 2026.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As EV batteries for e-taxis may need to be replaced around the five-year mark, this extension will enable taxi operators to optimise their investments and price e-taxi rentals competitively.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In turn, our taxi operators have committed that at least half of our taxis will be electric by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This is a significant move, given our total taxi fleet of around 15,000 today.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Among private hire cars, 50% of GrabRentals fleet will also go electric by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: LTA will continue working closely with private hire car operators to increase EV adoption.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will make a similar concerted push for our public bus fleet.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We aim for half of our public buses to be electric by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This means an almost 50-fold increase from the 60 electric buses today, to about 3,000 by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To achieve this, bus buys from now till 2030 will primarily be electric.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For a start, LTA will replace over 400 diesel buses with electric buses by 2025.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To further green our public transport infrastructure, LTA will call a tender later this month to deploy more solar panels at locations like rail and bus depots, the upcoming Integrated Train Testing Centre, covered linkways and pedestrian overhead bridges.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This will reduce both emissions and energy costs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Goods vehicles and private buses are also key to our effort as they contribute the bulk of our remaining emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As Mr Dennis Tan noted, last year, MSE implemented the Commercial Vehicle Emissions Scheme and enhanced the Early Turnover Scheme to encourage the adoption of cleaner-energy light goods vehicles.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: However, for the heavier goods vehicles, there are fewer viable cleaner-energy solutions currently available.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will work closely with industry partners to track technology advancements in this space with a view towards early adoption of viable solutions for heavier goods vehicles.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Chairman, in summary, we are taking decisive action to reduce land transport emissions by 80% by or around mid-century.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But beyond these efforts, the success of this green endeavour, ultimately, rests with each one of us and the commuting decisions we make every day.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And if we walk or cycle, the carbon footprint is practically zero.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, we can make a difference with our choices.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: At the MOT COS debate, we will share more about our plans to make all these options more accessible by expanding the rail network, repurposing our roads and building more cycling paths.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our informed individual choices will have an indelible and enduring impact on our carbon footprint, environment and future.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Together, we can make the vision of the Singapore Green Plan a reality.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chairman, I will first give an update on our work to make our city more sustainable and how this will support our transition to a low-carbon economy and create opportunities for our firms and workers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, I will report on our progress to transform Singapore into a City in Nature.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And third, set out how we will strengthen our R&D to find innovative ways to improve our urban sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Let us start with how we are making our built environment and our city more sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, the work to green our buildings is very important.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As we do this, we also want to create growth opportunities for our companies and workers in our built environment sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have moved decisively to meet these targets over the past year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, let me share some updates on our progress and our plans to support the industry in this green transition, which Members like Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Prof Koh Lian Pin have asked about.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our first target is to green 80% of buildings by Gross Floor Area (GFA) by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we are well on our way to meeting our target.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we need to do more to sustain our momentum and push ahead.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last December, we raised the minimum energy performance requirements that both new buildings, as well as existing buildings undergoing major retrofitting, must now meet.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have also worked with our industry to revise the Green Mark scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have set higher energy efficiency standards and increased our emphasis on other sustainability outcomes, too, such as reducing carbon emissions across a building's lifecycle.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will help ensure that Singapore’s Green Mark remains one of the world's leading green building certifications and the go-to standard in the tropics.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we have raised both our minimum environmental sustainability requirements, as well as our standards at the higher end, for Green Mark.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In particular, we want to encourage owners of older buildings to retrofit them to be more energy-efficient, because these tend to be less resource- and carbon-intensive than demolishing them and constructing new ones.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our second target is for 80% of new developments to be Super Low Energy (SLE) buildings from 2030.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are buildings that achieve energy savings of over 60%, as compared to 2005 levels, when we started our journey to green our buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is a modest but promising start, as we bring SLE developments into the mainstream.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Government is taking the lead to make more buildings SLE buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under GreenGov.SG, we have raised our energy performance requirements for public sector buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: All new public sector buildings and existing ones undergoing major retrofitting must now meet Green Mark Platinum SLE standards.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are encouraging developers to pursue SLE standards, too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In November last year, we started an incentive scheme that will give developers of private projects bonus GFA, if they meet Green Mark Platinum SLE standards and other requirements.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also require higher environmental standards from developers for the new Government Land Sales (GLS) sites that we launch from the second quarter of this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If we want to achieve these ambitious targets, we must ensure that our firms and workers have the capability to design, build and maintain SLE buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have been building up a core of talent to support our sustainability efforts, as Mr Cheng Hsing Yao has mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As of September last year, we have worked with our partners to train more than 22,000 green professionals.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will work with training providers so that their courses cover the latest developments in sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through collaborative platforms like the Super Low Energy Building Smart Hub, we will also facilitate the sharing of new energy-efficient technologies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope that our firms and our professionals will make good use of these resources to upgrade their skills.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will share more on our plans to attract and upskill talent at MND's COS.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This brings me to our third target, which is to achieve 80% improvement in energy efficiency, compared to 2005 levels, for our best-in-class buildings by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, we have achieved some 65% to 70% improvement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To help us with this important effort, we have a programme under what we call the Green Buildings Innovation Cluster (GBIC).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This supports the research, prototyping and demonstration of our green building technologies and encourages companies to adopt these solutions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The SMU Connexion building uses a Passive Displacement Cooling system, which makes use of convectional currents to circulate cool air throughout most of the building.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This new technology can achieve energy savings of up to 40% over conventional air-conditioning systems.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is one of several technologies that enable the building to achieve Zero Energy standards, which means that its entire energy consumption is offset by renewable energy generated on-site.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To further push the boundaries of energy efficiency, we will enhance funding for GBIC by a further $45 million.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under GBIC 2.0, we want to target key demand drivers, such as building owners and developers, as well as their value chains, to jointly develop innovative solutions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These include energy-efficient cooling technologies, smart building systems and enhanced building ventilation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will accelerate the commercialisation of these solutions through industry partnerships and help to grow the local ecosystem of firms with green building expertise.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This way, our companies can compete better in serving the growing global demand for sustainable urban solutions and take the lead to drive sustainable development across the Asia Pacific, home to some of the fastest-growing economies in the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond individual buildings, Members have asked how we will make our HDB towns more sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will do this by tapping on new technologies and smart infrastructure solutions under our HDB Green Towns Programme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will complement the various initiatives that MSE is piloting in the Eco Towns.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, for new HDB flats, we are using green technologies, such as smart lighting for common areas, as well as rainwater harvesting systems, to reduce energy consumption and the use of potable water.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Hany Soh asked whether we use green construction methods for our HDB Home Improvement Programme (HIP) upgrading works.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We require all builders for our HIP projects to come under the Green and Gracious Builders Scheme, which sets standards to mitigate the environmental impact of construction work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB also adopts other green construction practices, such as reusing metal hoardings for future projects.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have also been installing solar panels on top of our existing HDB blocks to power common services, such as lifts and lighting.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we will strive to install solar panels on as many HDB blocks as possible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond this, we are also exploring how to make good use of our limited space to enhance Singapore’s food security.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Poh Li San and Mr Don Wee asked how we can support more urban farms on the rooftops of multi-storey carparks (MSCPs).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Although the expected production volume is not very high or large, it will contribute to our “30 by 30” food production goal.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will be evaluating the outcomes of this programme first before we decide on future plans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Next, we are piloting some new initiatives in our HDB estates to encourage residents to live more sustainably.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For instance, we will introduce e-waste recycling bins in our HDB estates to make recycling more convenient.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will also support our Green Plan efforts to help Singaporeans recycle more and recycle right, as Minister Grace Fu had shared with us earlier.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also exploring the use of Light Emitting Surfaces (LES) for signages in our housing estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: LES is a new technology that can potentially reduce about 80% of energy consumption, compared to standard fluorescent block signages.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope that these initiatives will enable our residents to lead more sustainable lifestyles and leave a lower carbon footprint.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To finance the building of green and sustainable homes, HDB has also developed a Green Finance Framework.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: New HDB projects that seek to achieve BCA's Green Mark GoldPlus certification or above can now be financed or refinanced with green bonds or loans under this framework.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will support HDB as it seeks to reduce carbon emissions and energy consumption in our projects.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB's Green Finance Framework will also contribute to our whole-of-Government effort to further develop the green bond market in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked how we balance conservation and development.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will give a fuller update on our approach at MND's Committee of Supply later but let me briefly share some of the progress that we have made.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we have restored and enhanced several core habitats throughout the island.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These comprise over 12 hectares of forest, marine and coastal habitats in Singapore which are key ecosystems and important homes for native biodiversity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our latest studies have shown that many of our native flora and fauna species have become less threatened over time, such as the Smooth-coated Otter and the Lesser Mousedeer.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, beyond our core habitats, we have greened other parts of our city more intensively.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have established more nature parks, especially at the fringe of our core biodiversity areas, as ecological buffers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the past two years, we have announced new nature parks, such as the Khatib Bongsu Nature Park, a rich mangrove and mudflat habitat, and the Rifle Range Nature Park, a key buffer for our Bukit Timah Nature Reserve.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last year, we also added new parks at Bukit Gombak and Pasir Panjang and enhanced existing ones, such as the Coastal Playgrove at East Coast Park, with more lush vegetation and natural landscapes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have even expanded the greenery on our rooftops and facades of buildings and in our sky gardens, to over 140 hectares.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are well underway to meeting our target of 200 hectares of skyrise greenery by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked how we will make our green spaces accessible to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The moves we have made as part of City in Nature not only help nature to thrive in our city state but also bring all Singaporeans closer to our green spaces for all its benefits.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our City in Nature efforts can also help us build up our climate resilience through nature-based solutions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we have already begun to weave natural designs and plantings into our parks and streetscapes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By planting different shrubs and trees to mimic the multi-tiered structure of a natural forest, we can better connect our green spaces for animals like birds and butterflies and also beautify our city, provide shade, cool our surroundings and improve our air quality.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We can also use nature-based solutions to help protect our coastlines from rising sea levels.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Looking ahead, as Minister Grace Fu had shared earlier, research and innovation will enable us to achieve a low-carbon future.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to invest in science and technology for our city and our natural spaces.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To support our City in Nature ambitions, we have invested in R&D under our Cities of Tomorrow (CoT) and the Marine Climate Change Science (MCCS) programmes to explore solutions that tap on nature to help strengthen our ecological, climate and social resilience.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In one project, researchers created "green seawalls" that enhance our marine ecosystems at the same time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Cities of Tomorrow R&D programme will also improve our urban sustainability, such as by designing greener buildings for our tropical climate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For instance, air-conditioning uses a lot of energy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: BCA and NUS are exploring the use of weather sensors and smart watches that track how building occupants respond to indoor conditions to optimise cooling and ventilation systems.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will support us in developing innovative solutions for a more sustainable, liveable and resilient city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Whether it is making our built environment and city more sustainable or transforming Singapore into a City in Nature, we all need to work together – Government agencies, industry partners, academics and researchers, nature groups and the wider community.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While we have made good progress so far, there is much more to do and we must press on in close partnership.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Along the way, we can help local firms and our workers build expertise in sustainability solutions and create good jobs and good opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we can grow a greener and more sustainable home for all of us – one where we live in harmony with nature as good stewards of our environment for generations to come.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE has been making good progress since the announcement of the Eco-Stewardship Programme, or ESP, last year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Through the "4Cs" approach of Curriculum, Campus, Culture and Community, we continue to holistically nurture our students from Primary to pre-University levels to be environmental stewards for our future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continue to support our teachers for the ESP through professional development opportunities and teaching resources on sustainability in the Student Learning Space.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE is also developing an Eco-Stewardship Toolkit, which will include a repository of resources to further support schools in strengthening their sustainability journey.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I agree with Ms Foo Mee Har that our institutions play a critical role in Singapore's green transition.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As part of our Green Plan effort, our institutions have made sustainability a strategic priority in their agendas, with some of our Autonomous Universities developing comprehensive masterplans on their sustainability targets and initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: One, leveraging their research and innovation capabilities to develop new products and services which enable other sectors of our society to tackle sustainability challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Two, developing the skills and competencies of our graduates and the workforce to enable them to seize opportunities in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The deep research and innovation capabilities of our institutions position them well to advance Singapore's sustainability goals.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In tandem with their hands-on approach to sustainability education, our institutions partner companies, agencies and our community on research and innovation projects that advance national sustainability efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, our institutions can develop innovative solutions to support the industry's green transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Through projects that they work on with the industry, the Polytechnics enable local enterprises to reduce their carbon emissions and achieve sustainability goals.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, in January this year, Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP) launched a Sustainability Experience Centre in partnership with Schneider Electric, a company specialising in energy and automation digital solutions for efficiency and sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In partnership with a local startup, Firmbase Private Limited, Ngee Ann Polytechnic's Environmental and Water Technology Centre of Innovation has recently developed a membrane for effective oil-water separation in the treatment of oily wastewater in the oil and gas industry.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, our Autonomous Universities are leveraging their deep research capabilities for sustainability R&D and using their own campuses as "living laboratories" to support national research and talent development efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, Nanyang Technological University (NTU) has partnered France's Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission, or CEA, to set up the Singapore-CEA Alliance for Research in the Circular Economy, focusing on research around recycling of electronic waste.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As part of its Sustainability Plan, Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) will be transforming its campus in Changi into a green experimental ground.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will allow SUTD faculty and students to partner the industry and the community to testbed new technologies and innovative projects for sustainable and smart living.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Such studies may include waste management and reducing electricity usage.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our institutions also play an important role in equipping our youth and workforce with the skills and competencies for the growing green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We can expect more new jobs to emerge and more exciting jobs to adopt green practices.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We, therefore, need to invest in "green upskilling" for our workforce so that they can seize the new opportunities presented by green growth.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our institutions are refreshing their specialised course offerings and are launching new programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These programmes provide young Singaporeans with forward-looking skills for emerging green jobs or existing jobs that are going to be "greened".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, Republic Polytechnic recently launched the Diploma in Environmental and Marine Science, which prepares students to take up roles at the forefront of developing sustainable, environmental and aquaculture solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond equipping students to enter green jobs, we are also equipping the broader base of students with knowledge, competencies and skills related to sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Almost all our institutions include sustainability as a theme for their common curricula for undergraduates.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Singapore Management University, for instance, offers a common module on "Climate Change, Global and Local Solutions" as part of its core curriculum for undergraduates.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our institutions will continue to work closely with industry partners to curate more internship opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will expand the offerings in our institutions to meet the market demand and our students' aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Chairman, to conclude, MOE is fully committed to contribute to a sustainable Singapore under the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our schools will be a key foundational enabler for this journey, as they nurture the next generation of our students to be stewards in environmental sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our institutions will play significant, needle-moving roles by building up their capabilities and capacities, in partnership with the industry.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They will leverage their research and innovation capabilities to develop sustainable products and solutions and equip our graduates and workforce with in-demand and emerging green skills.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, it takes a whole-of-nation effort to make sustainability our way of life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We, therefore, welcome experts, educators, companies, community partners and all Singaporeans to join in this endeavour to embrace sustainability consciousness and practices, build skills for the green economy and develop innovative solutions to create a greener and lasting future for generations to come.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Eco Fund is actually designed to allow very broad-based participation and it is made very inclusive for different types of groups.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Individuals, businesses, community, grassroots organisations or charities can participate.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Actually, it allows groups to participate in a wide area of interests.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It stretches across all the five pillars of the Singapore Green Plan.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The key indication that we are looking for in all these groups is whether they are able to mobilise the community around them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That is the key that we are looking for.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Chairman, I would like to thank the Senior Minister and the Ministers for their very detailed answers to some of our cuts.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: My first clarification is with regard to the risk-weighted assets question that I asked in my cut.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: With the efforts to incentivise carbon credits and the ecosystem, may I ask Minister for Trade and Industry Mr Gan Kim Yong whether the efforts to incentivise by introducing risk-weighted assets are a bit lower for FIs, for example, to hold on to carbon credits?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: As of now, I think carbon credits are regarded as a high risk and the weights in the risk-weighted asset are quite high.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: For my second clarification, I would like to first thank Minister for Transport S Iswaran for sharing that the cut-off for EV cars for COE Cat A has been increased to 110 kilowatts, thus benefiting 10 cars.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: But my question is with regard to my cut about the taxes – road tax for EVs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Can the Minister share a bit more how we can enhance this incentivisation of the rebate structure for EV cars on the road tax front?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And the other one is on motorcars – what monitoring developments and assessments will be needed to ensure that earlier adoption incentive for electric motorcycles can be done earlier than later?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In fact, banks do have exposure to carbon credits, for example, from trading in carbon credits arising from a market intermediary.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Banks, therefore, can be exposed to the risk of losses arising from market movements in the price of carbon credits.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will continue to work with the financial institutions to see how we can better quantify the risks so that we can manage risk-weighting better.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for his questions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If I may take the second one on electric motorcycles first.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I have said earlier in my speech, the technology is still evolving, different models, different types of solutions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we are tracking this very closely and we will make an assessment of the need to put in place any specific measures that might facilitate earlier or quicker adoption of such e-motorcycles.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Member's first question was around incentives for electric cars and, in particular, the road tax angle.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, let me address this in three parts.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As the Member would be aware, last year, we made a series of changes to the road tax treatment of EVs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As a result of that, the road tax payable by mass- to mid-market EVs is, generally, in line with their ICE equivalents.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that does not seem to be an impediment per se, but we will continue to monitor this and see if there is a need for further tweaks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, when we put these together with the recurrent costs – and the likely savings in recurrent costs of running an EV, because the maintenance tends to be less costly and so on – we think that, on balance, the economics works in favour of EV adoption or, at least, not against it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But we will continue to monitor this because this is an evolving space.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But if I may make a final point, Mr Chairman, I think it is important to bear in mind that EVs are, first and foremost, vehicles; hence, "V"s.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that means our policies on car ownership, usage and, indeed, the emphasis on a car-lite strategy and greater use of public transport – those must remain as important principles that guide our larger transport policies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we want to encourage the adoption of EVs in the context of our larger green transition, but we also want to ensure that, where we can and where it is also within the ken of our people, greater transition to the use of public transport and less carbon-emitting modes of transportation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Chairman, I would like to seek two clarifications from Minister Gan Kim Yong.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The first one is on the projects of the sustainable Jurong Island project because, currently, most of all the projects and the carbon emissions are based on disclosures by the industry or the companies.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The second question is with regard to the new technologies that we are going to bring across, whether on Jurong Island or in Singapore, how will we be doing this sandbox of the new pilots?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Could the Minister elaborate further on how this would be possible so that people with good proposals would put them up?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is something that we will continue to work with the industry on and to develop the standards for that.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Miss Cheryl Chan also asked about how we embark on sandbox projects.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: EDB, ESG and A*STAR are working very closely with industries and looking at the various new technologies, new solutions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We welcome industries, companies or researchers who are interested in the respective areas of green projects to discuss with us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For the small and medium enterprises (SMEs), it would be easier for them to approach ESG to talk about potential projects and the various schemes that will be available that they can tap on to embark on these projects.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And for the larger projects, like CCUS and so on, they can talk to EDB as well as A*STAR, which has a centre which I mentioned that they have set up with regard to carbon utilisation and technology.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask that we consult with the NGOs and activists sooner rather than later because they have shared with me that they were consulted rather late when it came to the carbon tax increase?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: The first one is for the Senior Minister.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: The Senior Minister mentioned that about 5,000 companies now have given their commitment towards the decarbonisation solution.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: On the second question, the Senior Minister and Minister Gan Kim Yong also shared about some of these new and nascent technologies, such as carbon capture and hydrogen, that we are now studying to open up our own technologies for future renewable energies.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: So, I would like to understand more about do we have any plans to devote more of our resources, our Budget, to investments in such energy, new nascent energy and technologies.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Some of these facilities will require also large amounts of land to build them.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Do we have plans to adjust our land use plans to accommodate such facilities?

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: On the first question, I do not have a count of how many of the 5,000 which have committed to net-zero in COP26 are actually in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: But we do know that there are many companies in Singapore – international companies and major ones.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Minister Gan Kim Yong has given the example of Shell, which is a major E&C company, which has made a commitment to go to net-zero by 2050 – Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: They have been long-time residents here in Singapore, contributing greatly to our economy and we will partner them.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: A number of other companies – ExxonMobil, for example, has committed to going net-zero in its operations by 2050.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: They are very interested in CCU as a technology.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Both companies are very interested in developing Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAF) and other forms.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: There are other important companies in Singapore like Neste, which is a major producer of biodiesel.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We have one of the biggest plants in the world, if not the biggest plant in the world.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: And they have expressed an interest in expanding their range of products here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: So, there are a number of useful opportunities.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Minister Gan Kim Yong may want to add to that.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I mentioned this in my remarks earlier on that we have devoted quite a lot of resources into the development of technology and R&D.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are also consolidating the various institutions under A*STAR so that we can create greater synergy among these research efforts to focus on investment in the development of these technologies.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But I must add that many of these technologies are still very nascent and they are in the developmental stage.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will need to continue to remain nimble and monitor their development, keep pace with their development not only in Singapore but globally, and explore collaboration with international institutions, research institutions, so that we are able to keep tabs on the latest development in the technology and seek collaboration in developing some of these capabilities.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I also agree with the Member that it is important for us to also invest in building capability among our people, as well as I have also mentioned about training and upgrading.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Minister Chan Chun Sing talked about education and how we equip our people to be able to invest their resources into R&D and also to capitalise on the employment opportunities that will be brought about by some of these emerging technologies.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I have one clarification for Minister Gan Kim Yong.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: My question relates to the new Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS-Green) to support local firms with a range of financing needs.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister if ESG would look into the feedback from the industry for FIs to look into more favourable terms for the EFS-Green to spur adoption.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: This is especially if the Government is risk sharing at 70%.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But as some of you might realise, many of us are wearing green in this House today.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In fact, it is the first time I am not wearing my white shirt in this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And I should thank Speaker, the Chairman, for also greening Parliament, for turning up the heat during our debates in this Chamber, and, by that, I mean turning up the temperature in the air-conditioning and also phasing out the use of single-use plastic bottles.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But we are not just wearing green today; I am glad and, hand on heart, we are truly going green.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, amidst a 24oC setting, is the hon Member given leave to withdraw the amendment?
